tasks.short: Contact customers to understand their needs and discuss suitable services.

steps.what: Review account history, open opportunities and outstanding service issues.
Arrange a discussion with the customer.
Discuss needs, explain service options and agree next steps.
Write customer notes from the discussion.

loop.input: Seller-entered discovery bullets and agreed next steps.
loop.output: Customer notes separating stated needs, commitments and unresolved questions.
loop.check: The seller checks commitments and names against the original bullets before saving.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction; missing or disputed facts return to the seller.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text discovery findings vary; a fixed template alone cannot condense them reliably.

steps.what: Create follow-up tasks with owners and deadlines.

tasks.design: Configure an account brief in the {CRM}, linked to the {HELPDESK}, and scheduling through the {CALENDAR} for customers who have agreed to a discussion. A bounded loop turns seller-entered bullets into reviewed customer notes; structured next steps create tasks in the {CRM}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Account context crossed systems, and discovery findings remained free text. The conversation itself depends on trust and changing customer needs.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing views and scheduling can be configured cheaply. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of connecting records and adding a small, checked drafting loop.
tasks.still_hard: Understanding unstated needs and recovering strained relationships remain human work. Contact permission, GDPR processing grounds and national outreach rules must be reflected in scheduling eligibility.
tasks.human_edge: Earn trust, notice hesitation and help customers express needs they have not yet articulated.

ambition.what: Weekly selection of accounts needing a new discovery conversation.

tasks.altitude: Preparation and paperwork take less of the week, leaving more time for discovery. The seller gains better evidence for choosing which accounts to revisit; formal decision rights do not change automatically.

reach.task: Translate discovery findings into a feasible service scope.
reach.learn: Learn service constraints, acceptance criteria and when technical discovery is needed.

evidence.claim: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Sales supports lead research and qualification, demonstrating account preparation capabilities.
Configured account views, scheduling and structured follow-up tasks need no autonomous agent.
Preparation can shrink while relationship-led discovery remains human; time estimates are planning assumptions.

assumptions: The company uses a {CRM} and has an approved service catalogue.
Automatic scheduling is restricted to customer-requested or already-agreed discussions.
Notes use seller-entered bullets; call recording is not required.
Step shares describe a typical contact cycle and are not measured customer data.
Build ranges cover a starter implementation; access and consultation can extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Whether account and service-ticket records share reliable identifiers.
Which contact permissions and processing grounds are recorded.
Which account fields the seller may access.
Whether national rules require employee consultation for the proposed changes.
research_questions: Which account facts actually change the seller's preparation?
Can existing scheduling configuration handle customer booking and cancellation?
Which discovery-note fields require explicit seller confirmation?
new_work: Review drafted customer notes and commitments.
Handle scheduling exceptions and incorrect account links.
Maintain brief fields, access rules and note templates.
Complete employee consultation under national rules where applicable.

tasks.short: Negotiate service prices and agreement terms with customers.

steps.what: Review the opportunity, current quote and existing agreement.
Calculate concession options and their margin effects.
Negotiate scope, price, timing and reciprocal commitments.
Request approval for concessions outside delegated limits.
Approve, reject or revise exceptional commercial terms.
Prepare revised terms from the authorised commercial position.
Check revised terms and send the commercial response.

tasks.design: A small scenario calculator joins approved costs and rate cards to the opportunity in the {CRM}, while the {WORKFLOW} routes concessions beyond delegated limits. Templates in the {CLM} generate revised terms from structured, authorised choices, and the seller approves the response before the {EMAIL} sends it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Costs, concession limits and agreements were scattered, making each negotiation pack expensive to assemble. Bargaining itself cannot be reduced to discount rules.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding makes a narrow calculator and approval integration cheaper to build. Existing templates and approval features handle the routine parts without a model.
tasks.still_hard: Service costs can be uncertain, and nonstandard clauses require specialist judgement. Commercial authority and agreement versions must stay aligned.
tasks.human_edge: Read the customer's priorities, trade concessions for reciprocal value and know when to walk away.

ambition.what: Same-day selection among scope, price and payment-term trade-offs.

tasks.altitude: The seller spends less time reconstructing economics and chasing approvals. Within existing delegated limits, they can compare and choose concession packages during the conversation; wider authority requires an explicit management decision.

reach.task: Evaluate concession requests against margin and account value.
reach.learn: Learn contribution margin, approval thresholds and how reciprocal commitments affect deal quality.

evidence.claim: Rate-card calculations and approval limits can be implemented with deterministic rules.
Teamleader provides commercial records and online quote signing, supporting the feasibility of connected agreement workflows.
Negotiation remains human while calculations, routing and templated responses can shrink.

assumptions: Most proposed changes use approved commercial options and clauses.
The seller records negotiated choices as structured fields.
Exception approvals are conditional; step shares average standard and exceptional negotiations.
Custom legal wording goes to a legal reviewer outside the standard template path.
Build ranges assume one service family and an existing approval policy.
unknowns: Whether current cost data supports useful margin calculations.
Who may approve discounts, payment changes and contractual exceptions.
Whether the {CLM} supports field-driven templates and version control.
Which access reviews or employee consultation national rules require.
research_questions: Which concessions recur often enough to encode as options?
Which cost uncertainties should appear as ranges in scenarios?
Can existing approval configuration replace approval requests in the {EMAIL}?
new_work: Maintain cost inputs, concession limits and approved clauses.
Review exceptional commercial packages and nonstandard wording.
Check that generated terms reflect authorised choices.
Monitor failed approval routing and outdated agreement versions.

tasks.short: Quote service prices, approved credit terms, contract terms and delivery dates.

steps.what: Read the customer request and identify required service details.

loop.input: Customer request and the approved service catalogue.
loop.output: Structured service, quantity, location, scope and requested-date fields with source references.
loop.check: Validate types and catalogue identifiers; the seller confirms scope and unsupported interpretations.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair; missing required fields return to the seller for clarification.
loop.why_not_simpler: Requests arrive as varied free text; deterministic parsing cannot reliably identify the intended service scope.

steps.what: Retrieve account terms, approved rates and applicable contract clauses.
Check available service capacity against the requested delivery date.
Confirm delivery commitments that exceed standard capacity rules.
Calculate service charges, discounts and applicable taxes.
Approve or reject pricing exceptions outside delegated limits.
Assemble the quote using approved prices, terms and dates.
Check the quote and send it to the customer.

tasks.design: A bounded loop extracts requests from the {EMAIL}; deterministic code joins rates and approved account terms from the {CRM} and {ERP} with capacity from the {OPS_SYSTEM}. The {WORKFLOW} routes commercial and delivery exceptions, then a template produces the quote using approved clauses from the {CLM}; the seller approves its release.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests were inconsistent, and pricing, credit terms and capacity came from separate sources. Bespoke integrations cost more than the repetitive quoting justified.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding makes narrow integrations and rate calculators cheaper. Bounded extraction handles request wording while code retains control of prices and terms.
tasks.still_hard: Bespoke scope, stale capacity and incomplete cost data can invalidate a quote. New credit decisions and nonstandard legal terms remain separate authorised processes.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve ambiguous scope and explain which service commitments matter to the customer.

ambition.what: Small customers needing same-day standard service quotes.

tasks.altitude: The seller handles more standard requests with less calculation and document assembly. They can choose among approved service configurations immediately; pricing exceptions and delivery overrides keep their existing approvers.

reach.task: Convert an accepted service quote into an accurate service order.
reach.learn: Learn order-ready scope fields, delivery dependencies and how to prevent quote-to-order mismatches.

evidence.claim: Salesforce Agentforce for Revenue can build quotes from a typed request.
Salesforce reports 75% less quoting time and 87% fewer clicks for its own sales team; the digest gives no base or period.
Deterministic rate calculations, templates and bounded request extraction support the proposed design; case results do not establish its savings.

assumptions: The starter covers a service family with explicit rates and approved clauses.
Credit terms are retrieved from existing approvals; no consumer creditworthiness is scored.
Standard dates follow authorised capacity rules; exceptional commitments require operations approval.
Approval-step shares average standard and exceptional quotes.
Where existing {CRM} configuration supports the calculation, configure it before building code.
GDPR applies to customer data; employee consultation follows national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Whether rate cards, tax rules and account terms have authoritative versions.
Whether capacity checks can reserve availability or require a freshness check before release.
Which quoting functions already exist in the {CRM}.
Who approves payment-term changes and nonstandard contract clauses.
Which access and consultation processes apply to the proposed implementation.
research_questions: What proportion of requests fit the standard service catalogue?
Which pricing and date errors cause the most rework?
Can configured quote templates and approval rules replace custom components?
Which request fields need clarification before any calculation starts?
new_work: Review extracted scope and approve quote release.
Handle missing requirements, pricing exceptions and capacity conflicts.
Maintain rate cards, taxes, clause versions and approval limits.
Monitor integration failures and stale capacity data.
Check generated quote lines against approved calculations after rule changes.

tasks.short: Maintain accurate customer and account records in connected systems.

steps.what: Collect approved customer changes and agreement details from source records.
Find the correct customer record and check for duplicates.
Update customer fields, account status and agreement references.
Copy approved billing changes into the customer finance record.
Update the parallel account tracker and reconcile copied fields.
Clarify conflicting details and resolve ambiguous customer matches.

tasks.design: Deterministic integrations collect approved structured changes from the {CRM}, {ERP} and {ESIGN}, match stable identifiers and update only permitted fields with an audit log on the {DATA_PLATFORM}. Ambiguous matches enter an exception queue in the {WORKFLOW}; shared views in the {CRM} replace the parallel tracker in the {SPREADSHEET}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Systems lacked consistent identifiers and field ownership, so sellers copied changes and kept a parallel tracker. Exception handling made integrations appear broader than they needed to be.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding reduces the cost of adapters, validation and retry handling. Existing matching, permissions and shared views can cover much of the work.
tasks.still_hard: Legacy duplicates, conflicting field ownership and restricted interfaces remain expensive. GDPR requires appropriate access, retention and processing grounds for customer data.
tasks.human_edge: Know when two records represent different buying relationships and verify changes that affect the customer.
tasks.altitude: Routine copying and tracker reconciliation largely leave the seller's week. They retain exception verification and gain time for customers; no new commercial decision rights arise from record automation.

reach.task: Validate new customer details before account activation.
reach.learn: Learn legal-entity identifiers, required account fields and the boundary between contact edits and sensitive finance changes.

evidence.claim: Teamleader provides customer records and online quote signing, showing that linked commercial records are available today.
Structured record updates, identifier matching and synchronisation can use deterministic integrations without a model.
A parallel tracker can be eliminated when its necessary fields and views exist in the authoritative system.

assumptions: Most updates come from structured, approved source fields, consistent with the task priors.
Free-text-only changes enter the human exception path rather than being guessed.
Automatic writes exclude bank details, new credit decisions and destructive record merges.
Billing changes have already received any required finance approval.
The parallel tracker contains copied fields rather than a distinct planning process.
Time shares and build ranges describe a starter design, not measured results.
unknowns: Which fields have authoritative owners across the {CRM} and {ERP}.
Whether stable customer identifiers exist and how many duplicates remain.
Whether signed agreement metadata is available as structured fields.
Whether the parallel tracker contains unique information.
Which write permissions, retention rules and national consultation requirements apply.
research_questions: Which source events can trigger updates without seller re-entry?
Can existing synchronisation configuration handle the permitted fields?
Which mismatches must block a write rather than generate a warning?
What prevents retiring the parallel tracker?
new_work: Resolve ambiguous identities and conflicting source values.
Monitor failed writes, retries and integration credentials.
Maintain field mappings, validation and retention rules.
Review access permissions and complete national employee consultation where applicable.
Verify that shared views cover the retired tracker's useful functions.

role.altitude: The seller's week shifts toward discovery, negotiation and resolving customer ambiguity. Better preparation and faster quotes support decisions within existing commercial limits; expanded authority requires explicit delegation.
reach: Sales engineer: turn discovery findings into feasible service scope.
Sales manager: compare concession economics and reciprocal commitments.
Order clerk: ensure accepted quotes contain order-ready information.
New accounts clerk: validate customer identity and account details.
skills_to_grow: Reading capacity constraints and delivery dependencies.
Checking model drafts against source facts.
Customer data quality, field ownership and GDPR-aware handling.
role.ambitious_version: A service seller who helps customers shape feasible options, compares commercial trade-offs during discussions and serves smaller accounts with prompt standard quotes, supported by reusable calculators, templates and integrations.

job.title: Sales Representatives of Services, Except Advertising, Insurance, Financial Services, and Travel
